```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wu_2023_mezigdomide"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wu_2023_mezigdomide"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13024> (open access; PMC10583261)

Mezigdomide (CC-92480) is an oral cereblon E3 ligase modulator in
development for multiple myeloma. Wu 2023 pooled two phase 1 single-dose
studies in healthy subjects to estimate the effects of a high-fat meal, of
the proton-pump inhibitor (PPI) rabeprazole and of a second formulation on
mezigdomide absorption. The final model (Table S2, run PK23) is a
two-compartment model with first-order absorption after a lag time. Food,
PPI and formulation act only on the absorption parameters (F, ka and Tlag);
none of them changes clearance or the volumes.

# Population

Sixty-four healthy subjects contributed 2038 plasma concentrations: 40 from
Study I (NCT03803644) and 24 from Study II (NCT04211545). Mean age was 38.5
years (range 18-55), mean weight 80.1 kg (54.8-103), and 90.6% were men.
By race, 56.3% were White, 40.6% Black or African American, 1.6% Asian and
1.6% American Indian or Alaska Native; 40.6% were Hispanic or Latino (Wu
2023 Table 1). Study I gave single fasted doses of 0.4, 0.8, 1.6 or 3.2 mg
(part 1, six subjects per dose), then 0.8 mg fasted and after an
FDA-standard high-fat meal in a two-period crossover (part 2, 16 subjects).
Study II gave 1.6 mg of formulation A and of formulation B in a randomized
crossover, then each formulation again after at least 7 days of rabeprazole
(four periods; Figure 1).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Wu_2023_mezigdomide")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every final estimate comes from Wu 2023 Figure 3a. That figure is a table
printed as an image, and it reports the random effects as standard
deviations (omega for IIV, gamma for IOV). The model stores variances.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lka` | log(1.18) 1/h | Figure 3a, ka pop |
| `ltlag` | log(0.423) h | Figure 3a, Tlag pop |
| `lcl` | log(35.1) L/h | Figure 3a, CL pop |
| `lvc` | log(440) L | Figure 3a, V1 pop |
| `lq` | log(36.8) L/h | Figure 3a, Q pop |
| `lvp` | log(243) L | Figure 3a, V2 pop |
| `lfdepot` | fixed(log(1)) | Figure 3a, F pop = 1 (fixed) |
| `e_fed_highfat_fdepot` | 0.234 | Figure 3a, beta F,FOOD |
| `e_form_mezigdomide_b_fdepot` | -0.236 | Figure 3a, beta F,FORMU |
| `e_conmed_ppi_fdepot` | -1.06 | Figure 3a, beta F,PPI |
| `e_fed_highfat_tlag` | 1.11 | Figure 3a, beta Tlag,FOOD |
| `e_fed_highfat_ka` | -1.15 | Figure 3a, beta ka,FOOD |
| `e_conmed_ppi_forma_ka` | -0.592 | Figure 3a, beta ka,PPIA |
| `e_conmed_ppi_formb_ka` | -1.99 | Figure 3a, beta ka,PPIB |
| `etalcl`, `etalvc` block | 0.399^2, 0.862 x 0.399 x 0.634, 0.634^2 | Figure 3a, omega CL, omega V1, corr V1,CL |
| `etalq` | 0.262^2 | Figure 3a, omega Q |
| `etalvp` | 0.255^2 | Figure 3a, omega V2 |
| `etaiov_ka_1` to `_4` | 0.650^2 | Figure 3a, gamma ka; Text S1 |
| `etaiov_tlag_1` to `_4` | 0.310^2 | Figure 3a, gamma Tlag; Text S1 |
| `addSd` | 0.0257 ng/mL | Figure 3a, error model a |
| `propSd` | 0.210 | Figure 3a, error model b |
| Covariate equations for log F, log ka, log Tlag; PPIA / PPIB definitions | n/a | Methods, 'Model development and methodology' |
| `d/dt(depot)`, `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(peripheral1)` | n/a | Text S1, structural model |
| `Cc ~ add(addSd) + prop(propSd) + combined2()` | n/a | Text S1, y = f + e sqrt(a^2 + b^2 f^2) |

# Virtual cohort

The observed data are not public. The simulation gives each of the eight
dose / treatment scenarios in Figure 2 its own cohort of 150 virtual
subjects. Each subject receives one single dose, so every record is on
occasion 1. With one occasion per subject, the occasion-level etas on ka and
Tlag act as between-subject variability, which is how the paper describes
them (Text S1: they combine IIV and IOV). The model has no demographic
covariates, so the cohorts need none.

```{r cohort}
scenarios <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario, ~dose, ~FED_HIGHFAT, ~CONMED_PPI, ~FORM_MEZIGDOMIDE_B,
  "0.4 mg, A, fasted", 0.4, 0, 0, 0,
  "0.8 mg, A, fasted", 0.8, 0, 0, 0,
  "0.8 mg, A, fed", 0.8, 1, 0, 0,
  "1.6 mg, A, fasted", 1.6, 0, 0, 0,
  "1.6 mg, B, fasted", 1.6, 0, 0, 1,
  "1.6 mg, A, fasted + PPI", 1.6, 0, 1, 0,
  "1.6 mg, B, fasted + PPI", 1.6, 0, 1, 1,
  "3.2 mg, A, fasted", 3.2, 0, 0, 0
) |>
  mutate(scenario = factor(scenario, levels = scenario))

n_per_arm <- 150L
obs_times <- c(
  0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16,
  24, 36, 48, 72, 96
)

make_cohort <- function(row, id_offset) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n_per_arm)
  dosing <- tibble(
    id = ids, time = 0, amt = row$dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"
  )
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(dosing, obs) |>
    mutate(
      scenario = row$scenario,
      dose = row$dose,
      FED_HIGHFAT = row$FED_HIGHFAT,
      CONMED_PPI = row$CONMED_PPI,
      FORM_MEZIGDOMIDE_B = row$FORM_MEZIGDOMIDE_B,
      OCC = 1L
    )
}

events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(scenarios)), function(i) {
  make_cohort(scenarios[i, ], id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_per_arm)
})) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Wu_2023_mezigdomide")
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20231024)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events,
  keep = c("scenario", "dose")
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(scenario = factor(scenario, levels = levels(scenarios$scenario)))

# Typical-value solve (no random effects) on a dense grid, one subject per
# scenario, for the closed-form AUC check below.
events_typical <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(scenarios)), function(i) {
  row <- scenarios[i, ]
  bind_rows(
    tibble(id = i, time = 0, amt = row$dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
    tibble(id = i, time = seq(0, 336, by = 0.05), amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    mutate(
      scenario = row$scenario, dose = row$dose,
      FED_HIGHFAT = row$FED_HIGHFAT, CONMED_PPI = row$CONMED_PPI,
      FORM_MEZIGDOMIDE_B = row$FORM_MEZIGDOMIDE_B, OCC = 1L
    )
}))
sim_typical <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
  events = events_typical,
  keep = c("scenario", "dose")
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(scenario = factor(scenario, levels = levels(scenarios$scenario)))
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 2: mean concentration-time profiles

```{r figure-2, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
# The pre-dose point (Cc = 0) cannot be drawn on a log axis.
sim |>
  group_by(scenario, dose, time) |>
  summarise(mean_Cc = mean(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    panel = paste(dose, "mg"),
    mean_Cc = ifelse(time == 0, NA_real_, mean_Cc)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, mean_Cc, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line(na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(size = 0.8, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.05, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  facet_wrap(~panel) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.01, 10)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 24, 48, 72, 96)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Mean mezigdomide concentration (ng/mL)",
    colour = "Scenario",
    title = "Mean simulated profiles by dose and scenario",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Wu 2023. Dashed line: LLOQ 0.05 ng/mL."
  )
```

The simulated means follow the published pattern. Concentrations rise
roughly in proportion to dose. After a high-fat meal the peak is later and
the AUC slightly higher. Rabeprazole lowers the curve markedly with either
formulation. All terminal phases run parallel, because no covariate acts on
disposition.

## Figure 5: visual predictive check

```{r figure-5, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
vpc_scen <- c(
  "0.4 mg, A, fasted", "0.8 mg, A, fasted", "0.8 mg, A, fed",
  "1.6 mg, A, fasted", "1.6 mg, A, fasted + PPI", "3.2 mg, A, fasted"
)
sim |>
  filter(scenario %in% vpc_scen) |>
  group_by(scenario, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q10 = quantile(Cc, 0.10),
    Q50 = quantile(Cc, 0.50),
    Q90 = quantile(Cc, 0.90),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q10, ymax = Q90), alpha = 0.25, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~scenario, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Mezigdomide concentration (ng/mL)",
    title = "Simulated median and 10th-90th percentiles",
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates the layout of Figure 5 of Wu 2023 (formulation A shown for",
      "the pooled 1.6 mg panels)."
    )
  )
```

## Figure 6: individual apparent clearance by dose level

```{r figure-6, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
sim |>
  filter(time == 0) |>
  distinct(id, dose, cl) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(paste(dose, "mg"), levels = paste(c(0.4, 0.8, 1.6, 3.2), "mg")), cl)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    x = "Dose level", y = "Oral clearance CL/F (L/h)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 6 of Wu 2023: CL/F does not depend on dose."
  )
```

# Food, PPI and formulation effects on relative bioavailability

No covariate acts on clearance. The AUC ratio between two scenarios at the
same dose therefore equals their ratio of relative bioavailability, which
is exp(beta). The typical-value solve must reproduce that ratio up to
numerical error, so this gate is tight.

```{r f-ratio}
typ_auc <- sim_typical |>
  arrange(scenario, time) |>
  group_by(scenario) |>
  summarise(
    auc = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2) +
      # Terminal extrapolation from the last two points (both in the beta phase).
      Cc[n()] / (log(Cc[n() - 1] / Cc[n()]) / (time[n()] - time[n() - 1])),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
auc_of <- function(s) typ_auc$auc[typ_auc$scenario == s]

# Exact closed form of the F ratio: AUC = F * dose / CL.
ini_vals <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$theta
f_ratio <- function(fed = 0, ppi = 0, formb = 0) {
  exp(ini_vals[["e_fed_highfat_fdepot"]] * fed +
    ini_vals[["e_conmed_ppi_fdepot"]] * ppi +
    ini_vals[["e_form_mezigdomide_b_fdepot"]] * formb)
}
typ_cl <- exp(ini_vals[["lcl"]])
auc_closed <- function(dose, ...) f_ratio(...) * dose / typ_cl * 1000

closed_check <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario, ~closed,
  "0.8 mg, A, fasted", auc_closed(0.8),
  "0.8 mg, A, fed", auc_closed(0.8, fed = 1),
  "1.6 mg, A, fasted", auc_closed(1.6),
  "1.6 mg, B, fasted", auc_closed(1.6, formb = 1),
  "1.6 mg, A, fasted + PPI", auc_closed(1.6, ppi = 1),
  "1.6 mg, B, fasted + PPI", auc_closed(1.6, ppi = 1, formb = 1)
) |>
  mutate(simulated = vapply(scenario, auc_of, numeric(1)))

# Trapezoidal AUC on a 0.05 h grid to 336 h with a log-linear tail; the
# remaining difference from F * dose / CL is numerical error.
stopifnot(all(abs(closed_check$simulated / closed_check$closed - 1) < 0.005))

ratios <- tibble::tribble(
  ~comparison, ~typical_sim, ~exp_beta, ~fig3b_model, ~fig3b_observed,
  "Fed / fasted (formulation A, 0.8 mg)",
  auc_of("0.8 mg, A, fed") / auc_of("0.8 mg, A, fasted"),
  f_ratio(fed = 1), 1.30, "1.29 (1.19-1.38)",
  "PPI / no PPI (formulation A, 1.6 mg)",
  auc_of("1.6 mg, A, fasted + PPI") / auc_of("1.6 mg, A, fasted"),
  f_ratio(ppi = 1), 0.360, "0.398 (0.321-0.493)",
  "PPI / no PPI (formulation B, 1.6 mg)",
  auc_of("1.6 mg, B, fasted + PPI") / auc_of("1.6 mg, B, fasted"),
  f_ratio(ppi = 1), 0.360, "0.373 (0.288-0.484)",
  "Formulation B / formulation A (1.6 mg)",
  auc_of("1.6 mg, B, fasted") / auc_of("1.6 mg, A, fasted"),
  f_ratio(formb = 1), 0.798, "0.820 (0.700-0.960)"
)

# Typical-value AUC ratio vs exp(beta): pure numerical error, so tight.
stopifnot(all(abs(ratios$typical_sim / ratios$exp_beta - 1) < 0.01))

ratios |>
  mutate(across(c(typical_sim, exp_beta), \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
  rename(
    "Comparison" = comparison,
    "Simulated typical AUC ratio" = typical_sim,
    "exp(beta) from Figure 3a" = exp_beta,
    "Figure 3b model-predicted F ratio" = fig3b_model,
    "Figure 3b observed AUCinf ratio (90% CI)" = fig3b_observed
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "AUC ratios between scenarios (Wu 2023 Figure 3b).")
```

The packaged model gives AUC ratios equal to exp(beta) from Figure 3a:
1.26 for fed over fasted, 0.346 with rabeprazole, and 0.790 for formulation
B over A. Figure 3b prints slightly different "model-predicted" ratios
(1.30, 0.360, 0.798), which exp() of the Figure 3a estimates does not give.
The Figure 3b caption defines its ratios as exp(beta), so they may come from
another run of the model. The differences are all under 4%. Every ratio,
from the Figure 3a estimates or from Figure 3b, lies inside the 90%
confidence interval of the clinically observed AUCinf ratio. The largest
gap between point estimates is for rabeprazole with formulation A: 0.346
from the model against 0.398 observed, 13% apart.

# PKNCA validation

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, scenario)

sim_nca <- bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> distinct(id, scenario) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, scenario, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, scenario, time)

dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, scenario)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | scenario + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | scenario + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  group_by(scenario, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)

nca_tab |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
  rename(
    "Scenario" = scenario,
    "Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax,
    "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "AUCinf (ng*h/mL)" = aucinf.obs,
    "t1/2 (h)" = half.life
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median simulated NCA parameters by scenario.")
```

Wu 2023 reports no NCA table. The Results give only the observed range of
Tmax: 1-4 h fasted without a PPI, and 4-8 h after the high-fat meal. The
check below compares the median simulated Tmax with those ranges. The
median is robust to which subjects land in the tails.

```{r tmax-check}
tmax_med <- setNames(nca_tab$tmax, as.character(nca_tab$scenario))
fasted_no_ppi <- c(
  "0.4 mg, A, fasted", "0.8 mg, A, fasted", "1.6 mg, A, fasted",
  "1.6 mg, B, fasted", "3.2 mg, A, fasted"
)
stopifnot(
  all(tmax_med[fasted_no_ppi] >= 1 & tmax_med[fasted_no_ppi] <= 4),
  tmax_med[["0.8 mg, A, fed"]] >= 4 & tmax_med[["0.8 mg, A, fed"]] <= 8
)
tmax_med
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Formulation labels.** The Methods call formulation A the reference
  (first-in-human) formulation and B the test formulation. The Figure 1
  caption swaps them. The model encodes the letter: `FORM_MEZIGDOMIDE_B = 1`
  for formulation B and 0 for A. This matches the paper's FORMU coding and
  its equations, which name the letter consistently.
- **Inter-occasion variability.** Monolix estimated occasion-level random
  effects on ka and Tlag and no separate IIV on them (Text S1). The model
  encodes this with one eta per occasion, for up to four occasions (Study II
  had four periods), each with the Figure 3a variance. Supply `OCC` = 1-4 per
  dosing period. A record with any other `OCC` gets no variability on ka or
  Tlag. The Discussion also lists random effects on F at the occasion level,
  but neither Text S1 nor Figure 3a contains such a term, so the model
  carries none.
- **Concentration units.** Doses are in mg and volumes in L. The model
  multiplies by 1000 so that `Cc` is in ng/mL, the unit of the assay (LLOQ
  0.05 ng/mL), of Figure 2 and of the additive residual SD.
- **Residual error.** Text S1 gives y = f + e sqrt(a^2 + b^2 f^2) (Monolix
  "combined2"). The model encodes it as `add(addSd) + prop(propSd) +
  combined2()`.
- **Narrative values that differ from Figure 3a.** The Discussion says the
  high-fat meal causes "a ~30% decrease in ka". But exp(-1.15) = 0.32, so ka
  falls to about 32% of its fasted value, a 68% decrease. The model uses the
  Figure 3a estimate. The Figure 3b "model-predicted" F ratios also differ
  slightly from exp(beta); see the ratio section above.
- **BLQ handling.** The paper treated BLQ samples (22.5%) as left-censored.
  Simulations here report the full predicted concentration. The
  sensitivity analysis that excluded BLQ data (Table S3) is not packaged,
  because the paper's final model is the censored fit in Figure 3a.
- **Screened covariates.** Weight, sex, serum creatinine and age were tested
  (Table S2, runs PK15-PK21) and not retained. They are listed in
  `covariatesDataExcluded`.
- **Literature check.** No correction notice was found for this article
  (Europe PMC search, 2026-10-27).
